notes.definition: Fish stocks in the oceans are declining. Sustainable fisheries keep fish stocks at a level where breeding continues, mainly by controlling net size and introducing fishing quotas.
explanation: Fish are an important source of food, especially protein, for people around the world. However, fish stocks in the oceans are declining. A fish stock is the population of a particular species of fish in an area that can be caught. When fish are caught faster than the remaining fish can breed to replace them, the stock falls. This is called overfishing.

It is important to maintain fish stocks at a level where breeding continues. If too many fish are removed, there are not enough adults left to reproduce, the population cannot recover, and certain species may disappear altogether in some areas. This would remove a food source for people and also affect other species in the food web that eat the fish or are eaten by them.

Control of net size plays an important role in conserving fish stocks. Nets with a larger mesh size let smaller, younger fish escape. These fish can then grow to maturity and breed before they are caught, so they produce the next generation. Nets with a small mesh catch fish of all sizes, including young fish that have never reproduced.

The introduction of fishing quotas also plays an important role. A fishing quota is a limit on the amount of a particular species of fish that can be caught in an area, usually set as a maximum mass per year. Quotas stop too many fish being caught, so enough adults are left to breed and the stock can stay stable or recover. Quotas can be lowered if a stock falls and raised if it recovers.

Together, these methods make fishing sustainable: enough fish can be caught now without reducing the ability of the stock to provide fish in the future. This links to food security, because sustainable methods must be found to feed everyone. Quotas can cause problems for fishing communities, as fewer fish caught can mean less income, but without them the stock, and the jobs that depend on it, could be lost completely.
keyFacts: Fish stocks in the oceans are declining.
Overfishing means catching fish faster than the stock can replace them by breeding.
Fish stocks must be maintained at a level where breeding continues.
If stocks fall too low, certain species may disappear altogether in some areas.
Control of net size: larger mesh lets young fish escape, grow and breed.
Fishing quotas limit the amount of each species that can be caught.
Net size control and quotas play important roles in conserving fish stocks.

keyTerms.definition: The population of a particular species of fish in an area that is available to be caught.
Catching fish faster than the population can replace them by breeding, so the stock declines.
A limit on the amount (usually mass) of a particular species of fish that can be caught in an area in a set time.
The size of the holes in a fishing net. A larger mesh lets smaller, younger fish escape.
Catching fish at a rate that allows the stock to keep breeding and remain at a stable level for the future.

workedExamples.title: Percentage decrease in a fish stock
workedExamples.question: A cod stock fell from 800 000 tonnes to 200 000 tonnes. Calculate the percentage decrease.

workedExamples.title: Will the stock grow?
workedExamples.question: A fish stock is 50 000 tonnes. Breeding and growth add 12% to the stock each year. The quota allows 4000 tonnes to be caught each year. Calculate the stock after one year.
steps: The stock has increased, so this quota is sustainable.

workedExamples.title: Effect of mesh size
workedExamples.question: A trawler using a small mesh net catches 2000 fish, of which 1400 are too young to have bred. Calculate the percentage of young fish and explain why a larger mesh would help.
steps: These young fish are removed before they can reproduce.
A larger mesh would let them escape, grow to maturity and breed.
workedExamples.answer: 70%; a larger mesh lets young fish escape so they can breed and maintain the stock.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think fish stocks will always recover on their own if fishing stops for a short time.
misconceptions.right: In fact if a stock falls too low there may be too few adults to breed, and the species may disappear altogether in that area.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think a larger net mesh catches more fish.
misconceptions.right: In fact a larger mesh lets smaller, younger fish escape so they can reach breeding age; it is a conservation method.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often describe a quota as a ban on fishing.
misconceptions.right: In fact a quota is a limit on how much of a species can be caught; fishing continues, but at a sustainable level.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think catching young fish is better because adults are left to breed.
misconceptions.right: In fact young fish have not yet bred, so removing them means fewer adults in the future to replace the stock.

realWorld: The North Sea cod stock fell to very low levels by the early 2000s. Strict quotas and other controls were then introduced, and the stock partly recovered.

The collapse of the Grand Banks cod fishery off Newfoundland in 1992 led to a fishing ban and the loss of thousands of jobs, showing what happens when a stock is not kept at a level where breeding continues.
Fisheries regulations set minimum mesh sizes for trawl nets so that young fish can escape.
separateOnlyContent: This whole subtopic (declining fish stocks, net size control and fishing quotas) is in separate Biology (8461) only. It is not assessed in Combined Science Trilogy (8464).
examTips: For net size, always explain the full chain: larger mesh → young fish escape → grow to maturity → breed → stock maintained.
For quotas, say they limit the amount of a species caught so enough fish remain to breed.
Use the specification phrase: fish stocks must be maintained at a level where breeding continues.
In data questions, use percentage change and compare the catch with how much the stock increases by breeding.
summary: Fish stocks in the oceans are declining because of overfishing.
Stocks must be kept at a level where breeding continues.
Otherwise some species may disappear altogether in some areas.
Larger net mesh sizes let young fish escape and breed.
Fishing quotas limit the amount of each species caught.
Sustainable fisheries help long-term food security.

questions.question: What is happening to fish stocks in the oceans?
options: They are increasing rapidly
They are staying the same
They are declining
They are no longer being fished
markScheme: 1 mark: they are declining
questions.explanation: Fish stocks in the oceans are declining because fish are being caught faster than they can breed to replace themselves.

questions.question: Which two methods play important roles in the conservation of fish stocks?
options: Control of net size and fishing quotas
Using smaller nets and fishing all year
Adding fertiliser to the sea and using bigger boats
Catching only young fish and releasing adults
markScheme: 1 mark: control of net size and fishing quotas
questions.explanation: These are the two methods named in the specification. Smaller nets and catching young fish would reduce stocks further.

questions.question: What is a fishing quota?
options: A ban on all fishing
The size of the holes in a net
A tax on fish sold in shops
A limit on the amount of a species of fish that can be caught
markScheme: 1 mark: a limit on the amount of a species of fish that can be caught
questions.explanation: A quota limits the catch; it does not ban fishing completely. Mesh size is a separate method.

questions.question: Why does increasing the mesh size of fishing nets help to conserve fish stocks?
options: Larger fish can escape and breed
Young, smaller fish can escape, grow and breed
Fishing boats use less fuel
More fish of every size are caught
markScheme: 1 mark: young, smaller fish can escape, grow and breed
questions.explanation: Larger holes let small, young fish pass through. They survive to adulthood and reproduce, replacing the fish that are caught. Larger fish are still caught.

questions.question: Why is it important to maintain fish stocks at a level where breeding continues?
options: So that fish grow larger
So that fishing boats can catch more each year
Otherwise certain species may disappear altogether in some areas
So that the sea does not become overcrowded
markScheme: 1 mark: otherwise certain species may disappear altogether in some areas
questions.explanation: If too few adults remain, the population cannot replace itself and the species may be lost from that area.

questions.question: What does overfishing mean?
options: Catching fish faster than the stock can replace them by breeding
Catching only one species of fish
Fishing with a large mesh net
Fishing in deep water
markScheme: 1 mark: catching fish faster than the stock can replace them by breeding
questions.explanation: Overfishing is about the rate of catching compared with the rate of reproduction. Large mesh nets reduce the effect of fishing on young fish.

questions.question: Scientists report that a haddock stock has fallen below the level at which breeding can replace the fish caught each year. Which action is most likely to allow the stock to recover?
options: Reduce the mesh size of nets
Increase the quota
Allow fishing in breeding areas
Reduce the quota for haddock
markScheme: 1 mark: reduce the quota for haddock
questions.explanation: A lower quota means fewer fish are caught, so more adults remain to breed. Increasing the quota or reducing mesh size would make the decline worse.

questions.question: Why might controlling net size on its own not be enough to conserve a fish stock?
options: Large mesh nets catch more young fish
There is no limit on how many adult fish are caught, so too few may be left to breed
Young fish cannot pass through any net
Net size has no effect on which fish are caught
markScheme: 1 mark: there is no limit on how many adult fish are caught, so too few may be left to breed
questions.explanation: Net size protects young fish, but if unlimited numbers of adults are caught the breeding population can still collapse. This is why quotas are also used.

questions.question: Young cod are small and adult cod are large. Which mesh size would be most suitable for fishing cod sustainably?
options: 10 mm
40 mm
120 mm
1 mm
markScheme: 1 mark: 120 mm
questions.explanation: The largest mesh lets the small young cod escape while still catching large adults. Smaller meshes would catch young fish before they can breed.

questions.question: What happens to small, young fish when the mesh size of a net is increased?
options: They are caught more easily
They are killed by the net
They are counted as part of the quota
They can escape through the holes in the net
markScheme: 1 mark: they can escape through the holes in the net
questions.explanation: Larger holes let small fish swim through, so they survive to grow and breed.

questions.question:
A cod stock fell from 800 000 tonnes to 200 000 tonnes.
Calculate the decrease in the stock.
questions.explanation: Subtract the final value from the starting value: 800 000 − 200 000 = 600 000 tonnes.

questions.question:
A cod stock fell from 800 000 tonnes to 200 000 tonnes.
Calculate the percentage decrease in the stock.
markScheme: 1 mark: 75%
questions.explanation: Percentage decrease = decrease ÷ original × 100 = 600 000 ÷ 800 000 × 100 = 75%. Dividing by 200 000 would give 300%, which is wrong.

questions.question:
Scientists recommend that no more than 15% of a mackerel stock is caught each year. The stock is 120 000 tonnes.
Calculate the maximum quota.
markScheme: 1 mark: 18 000 tonnes

questions.question:
A fish stock is 50 000 tonnes. Breeding and growth add 12% to the stock each year. The quota allows 4000 tonnes to be caught each year.
Calculate the size of the stock after one year.
markScheme: 1 mark: increase = 50 000 × 0.12 = 6000 tonnes
1 mark: 52 000 tonnes
questions.explanation: The stock gains 6000 tonnes and loses 4000 tonnes to fishing, so it rises to 52 000 tonnes. The quota is lower than the gain from breeding, so it is sustainable.

questions.question:
A trawler using a small mesh net catches 2000 fish. 1400 of them are too young to have bred.
Calculate the percentage of the catch that are young fish.
markScheme: 1 mark: 70%
questions.explanation: 1400 ÷ 2000 = 0.7, which is 70%. Most of the catch has never reproduced, which is why larger mesh sizes are needed.

questions.question:
A fish stock of 40 000 tonnes decreases by 10% each year because of overfishing.
Calculate the size of the stock after 2 years.
markScheme: 1 mark: after 1 year 40 000 × 0.9 = 36 000 tonnes
1 mark: after 2 years 36 000 × 0.9 = 32 400 tonnes
questions.explanation: Each year the stock is 90% of the previous year. 40 000 × 0.9 × 0.9 = 32 400 tonnes. Subtracting 20% of 40 000 (giving 32 000) is a common error because the second 10% is taken from the smaller stock.

questions.question: State what is happening to fish stocks in the oceans.
markScheme: 1 mark: they are declining / decreasing
questions.explanation: Fish stocks are declining, mainly because of overfishing.

questions.question: Name two methods used to conserve fish stocks.
markScheme: 1 mark: control of net (mesh) size
1 mark: fishing quotas
questions.explanation: These are the two methods in the specification.

questions.question: What is meant by a fishing quota?
acceptedAnswers: limit on amount of fish caught
limit on number of fish caught
markScheme: 1 mark: a limit on the amount / number of a species of fish that can be caught
questions.explanation: Quotas set a maximum catch for each species, usually as a mass per year.

questions.question: Explain how increasing the mesh size of fishing nets helps to conserve fish stocks.
markScheme: 1 mark: young / small fish can escape through the net
1 mark: so they survive to breed / reproduce and replace the fish caught
questions.explanation: The important link is that the escaped fish go on to breed, so the stock is maintained.

questions.question: Explain how fishing quotas help to conserve fish stocks.
markScheme: 1 mark: quotas limit the amount of fish that can be caught
1 mark: so enough fish are left to breed / the stock can be maintained or recover
questions.explanation: Quotas prevent overfishing by keeping the catch below the rate at which the stock can replace itself.

questions.question: Explain why it is important to maintain fish stocks at a level where breeding continues.
markScheme: 1 mark: if too few fish remain, there are not enough adults to breed / the population cannot replace itself
1 mark: so the species may disappear altogether in some areas (and fish will not be available as food in future)
questions.explanation: Breeding replaces the fish that are caught. Below a certain level, the stock cannot recover.

questions.question: Suggest why some people in fishing communities object to the introduction of strict fishing quotas, and give one argument in favour of quotas.
markScheme: 1 mark: fewer fish can be caught, so fishers earn less money
1 mark: jobs may be lost / boats may go out of business
1 mark: in favour: without quotas the stock could collapse, so there would be no fish (or jobs) in the future
questions.explanation: Quotas have short-term costs for fishing communities but protect the long-term future of the fishery.

questions.question: Explain why catching large numbers of young fish is particularly damaging to a fish stock.
markScheme: 1 mark: young fish have not yet bred / reproduced
1 mark: so there will be fewer adults in future to replace the fish caught / the stock declines
questions.explanation: Removing fish before they breed cuts off the next generation, so the stock cannot be maintained.

questions.question: Explain why sustainable fisheries are important for food security.
markScheme: 1 mark: fish are an important food (protein) source for many people
1 mark: keeping stocks at a breeding level means fish can still be caught in the future, so enough food is available
questions.explanation: Food security means having enough food to feed a population. If stocks collapse, an important food source is lost.

questions.question:
Fish stocks in the oceans are declining.
Describe and explain how fish stocks can be conserved, and explain why it is important to conserve them.
markScheme: Indicative content:
overfishing: fish caught faster than they can breed to replace themselves
stocks must be maintained at a level where breeding continues
otherwise certain species may disappear altogether in some areas
fish are an important food source; loss threatens food security and fishing jobs
loss of fish also affects other species in food webs
control of net size: larger mesh lets young / small fish escape
young fish then grow to maturity and breed, replacing those caught
fishing quotas limit the amount of each species that can be caught
so enough adults remain to breed and the stock can recover
quotas can be adjusted as stocks change
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): both methods clearly explained in terms of breeding, with a clear explanation of why conservation matters.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): both methods described with some explanation, or one method well explained with reasons for conservation.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): a method named or a simple reason for conservation.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Link every method to breeding. Examiners reward the full chain: method → more fish survive to breed → stock maintained → species and food source not lost.

questions.question:
The mass of a cod stock in an area was:
1980: 300 000 tonnes
1990: 180 000 tonnes
2000: 60 000 tonnes
2010: 90 000 tonnes
Strict quotas and a larger minimum mesh size were introduced in 2000.
Describe the trend in the data and explain the changes.
markScheme: Indicative content:
stock decreased from 1980 to 2000 (from 300 000 to 60 000 tonnes, an 80% fall)
caused by overfishing: fish caught faster than they could breed
stock increased from 2000 to 2010 (to 90 000 tonnes)
quotas limited the amount caught, so more adults remained to breed
larger mesh let young fish escape, grow and breed
stock still well below 1980 level: recovery is slow
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): trend described with data and both parts explained using quotas, mesh size and breeding.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): trend described simply, or one change explained.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Quote figures from the data when describing a trend, then explain each part using biology: overfishing for the fall and the conservation methods for the rise.
